findings.target: internal/logbook/types.go (Instant.UnmarshalJSON) × client lib/src/ui/app_fields.dart:23 pickLogDate → lib/src/logbook/trip.g.dart start/end
findings.finding: The client's only date input produces a NON-UTC DateTime, and a non-UTC DateTime encodes with NO ZONE SUFFIX. The server refuses it. `showDatePicker` returns `DateTime(y,m,d)` in the device's local zone; `_addDates` (trip_screen.dart:90-110) passes it straight to `setTripDates` with no `.toUtc()`; `trip.g.dart` writes `instance.start?.toIso8601String()`, and Dart emits `2027-10-12T00:00:00.000` — no `Z`, no offset — for a non-UTC value. `Instant.UnmarshalJSON` parses with `time.Parse(time.RFC3339, …)`, which requires an offset. So the two controls that set a trip's dates (T4 'Add dates', and T3 Create trip if it ever collects them) fail on every request. This is invisible to every leg the plan schedules, because `client_sample_log.json` was built with `DateTime.utc(...)` and every one of its date strings carries a Z — DEC-68's 'byte-identical golden round-trip per date-bearing field' is measured against exactly the data that cannot expose this.
findings.evidence: LIVE, against 127.0.0.1:8080: `PUT /v1/trips/lens-dates` with `"start":"2027-10-12T00:00:00.000"` → `400 {"code":"invalid_body"}`. The identical body with `...000Z` → `200`. Unit-level, in `internal/logbook`: `time.Parse(time.RFC3339, "2027-10-12T00:00:00.000")` → `cannot parse "" as "Z07:00"`; `json.Unmarshal` of that string into `TripWrite` → `logbook: "2027-10-12T00:00:00.000" is not an RFC 3339 instant`. Client side: `grep -rn 'toUtc' 'lib/src/screens/'` returns nothing, and `pickLogDate`'s result reaches `Trip.start` in three hops with no conversion.
findings.fix: Decide which side converts and write it down, because both are defensible and only one should happen. (a) CLIENT: the API layer normalises every DateTime with `.toUtc()` before encoding — right, because a trip's dates are calendar days and the log already treats them as midnight UTC everywhere else. Note this also changes what `logbook.json` holds today, so it is a local-format change as well as a wire one. (b) SERVER: `Instant.UnmarshalJSON` falls back to `time.Parse("2006-01-02T15:04:05.999", …)` as UTC when RFC3339 fails — cheap, but it silently reinterprets a zoneless string, which is the class of guess `logbookFormatVersion` exists to refuse. Recommend (a), plus a server leg that asserts a zoneless date is REFUSED rather than guessed. Either way add a golden leg whose input is a zoneless string, since no fixture can supply one.

findings.target: DEC-85 × DEC-32 — internal/logbook/types.go Trip.ShareLinkID, and the client's H1 (lib/src/screens/share_sheet_screen.dart:183-228)
findings.finding: DEC-85 names the cost as 'a RESTORED device shows a live link as not-shared'. The cost is larger than that and it is not restricted to restores: DEC-32's write response is a whole `Trip` the phone SPLICES into its cached log, and that Trip carries `shareLinkId: null`. So an ordinary rename, an 'Add dates', or a T5 itinerary change on a SHARED trip overwrites the local plaintext token with null — and the client holds the only copy, because the server now holds a hash. H1 then renders no URL (`url = trip.shareLinkId == null ? … : 'travellog.app/l/${trip.shareLinkId}'`), 'Copy link' and 'Stop sharing' both go inert (`onPressed: !trip.isShared || _busy ? null : _stop`), while the row in `share_links` is still un-revoked and `GET /l/{token}` still serves it. The user loses the capability AND the only control that revokes it, from an action that has nothing to do with sharing. `Trip.withName`'s own doc comment states the invariant this breaks, verbatim: 'renaming a trip you have shared must not quietly kill the URL somebody is holding.' The plan's guard cannot see it — the definition_of_done leg is "DEC-32's splice: the write's answer spliced into the cached document decodes equal to the next whole read", and the next whole read also has `shareLinkId: null`, so the leg is green while the token is destroyed.
findings.evidence: LIVE: `PUT /v1/trips/lens-dates` → `{…,"shareLinkId":null,…}` (200). `GET /v1/logbook` → the same. `internal/logbook/types.go:60-72` still declares the key, so it is emitted as an explicit null rather than omitted — the client's `json['shareLinkId'] as String?` accepts it, which is why this is data loss and not a crash. Client: `share_sheet_screen.dart:183-185, 222, 227-228`; `trip.dart:104` `bool get isShared => shareLinkId != null`.
findings.fix: Emit a non-secret derivation beside the hash: add `"shared": bool` to the emitted Trip, computed as `EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM share_links WHERE traveller_id=$1 AND trip_id=t.id AND revoked_at IS NULL)`. It leaks no capability, it restores `isShared` and therefore 'Stop sharing' from any device, and it costs one correlated subquery on a query already ordered by id. The client's `Trip.isShared` becomes `shared` rather than `shareLinkId != null`, and H1 gains a third state it does not have today: shared, but this device does not hold the link — 'New link' is the way back, which H1 already offers. This is an ADDITIVE field with a default, so it does not move the format version by the client's own rule. Whatever is chosen, the splice must be a merge that preserves `shareLinkId` rather than a replacement, and the leg must be written against a trip that HAS a live link — the current leg uses one that does not.

findings.target: internal/logbook/emit.go, and the file lists of steps R6 and R7 in docs/plan-v7.json
findings.finding: The definition_of_done carries the right rule — 'EVERY ROUTE THAT ANSWERS A BARE ENTITY GOES THROUGH AN EmitX FUNCTION' — and no step has a file to land it in. `emit.go` appears in NO step's file list; only `EmitTrip` exists. Measured, the two remaining shapes are exactly the defect `EmitTrip` was written for: a bare `Place` marshals `"visits":null` and a bare `Walk` marshals `"points":null`, and the client reads both as `(json['visits'] as List<dynamic>)` / `(json['points'] as List<dynamic>)` — non-nullable, no null branch, throws. `PUT /v1/places/{id}` (R6) answers a Place; `PUT /v1/walks/{id}` (R7) answers a Walk. `PUT /v1/cities/{id}` and `PUT /v1/photos/{id}` are safe because neither entity carries a list — worth stating so nobody adds two functions that are noise.
findings.evidence: Measured in `internal/logbook` (probe test, removed after): `bare Place marshals -> {…,"visits":null,…}`; `bare Walk marshals -> {…,"points":null,…}`; `bare City` and `bare Photo` carry no list key; `EmitTrip(zero) -> {…,"cityIds":[],…}`. Client codecs: `place.g.dart:33-35`, `photo.g.dart:46-48`. Plan: `python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('docs/plan-v7.json'));print([f for s in d['steps'] for f in s['files'] if 'emit' in f.lower()])"` → `[]`. `emit.go`'s own comment records that the `cityIds` version of this cost a defect against the running server.
findings.fix: Add `internal/logbook/emit.go (EDIT — EmitPlace, EmitWalk)` to R6's and R7's file lists, and state in the same breath that City and Photo need none and why. The AST sweep the definition_of_done promises is what stops a nineteenth route reintroducing it; write it in R6 rather than R8, since R6 is the first step that can violate the rule.

findings.target: the 18 unbuilt routes × the client's delete semantics (lib/src/logbook/logbook.dart:117, 154, 199)
findings.finding: Every route this plan has not built yet answers `{"code":"not_found"}` — the same word the vocabulary uses for 'that trip is not in your log'. There is no word for 'this build does not have that route'. Two consequences, and the second is the bad one. (1) A client build ahead of the server tells the user their trip/place/photo/walk is GONE, on 18 routes, and `NotFoundScreen` says exactly that. (2) `deletePhoto`, `removePlace` and `deleteTrip` all treat an unknown id as a SUCCESS by decision — 'the caller asked for that photo to be absent and it is'. The obvious network mapping of that rule (`not_found` → true) makes a delete against an undeployed route report success and delete nothing, and the client then advances its cache. R5, R6 and R7 each ship deletes, so this is live for the whole rollout rather than a corner.
findings.evidence: LIVE, against a server at R1 entry state: `DELETE /v1/trips/{id}` → `405 {"code":"not_found"}`; `PATCH /v1/me` → `404 {"code":"not_found"}`; `PUT /v1/places/x` → `404 {"code":"not_found"}`. Note the status and the code DISAGREE on the 405s (`internal/httpx/mux.go:89` returns the same prebuilt body for both). Client: `logbook.dart:117-119` `if (log.photo(id) == null) return Future<bool>.value(true);` and the same shape at 154-156 and 199-201.
findings.fix: Two things, both cheap. (a) Make the client's API layer branch on the HTTP STATUS as well as the code: a 404/405 whose route is in the client's own route table is a deployment mismatch, not a missing entity, and it must NOT be mapped to the delete-succeeded branch — it goes to the failure line. (b) Record in CLIENT-PREREQUISITES that the client must not ship a control ahead of its route, and give it a way to tell: the server already has `X-Logbook-Format`; a client that gets a 404 on a route it believes in should say 'this needs a newer server', not 'that trip is not in your log'. Consider whether the vocabulary wants a thirteenth word here — it is a real gap, and adding one is a DEC-12 decision rather than a patch.

findings.finding: PREVIOUSLY FOUND (v7.0) and RULED (DEC-76); re-measured here and confirmed unlanded, so it is still a blocker rather than a note. There is no version at which today's two builds exchange a document: the server stamps 2 and `Formats()` is `[2]`; the client compares `version != 1` with exact equality and QUARANTINES. Both directions measured live. What the re-measurement adds: the rest of the document is already conformant, so the version is the ONLY thing standing between the two — every other key, type and nullability on the whole 85 KB body passes the client's codec unchanged.
findings.evidence: LIVE: `GET /v1/logbook` → `"version": 2`; `GET /v1/logbook -H 'X-Logbook-Format: 1'` → `406 {"code":"unsupported_format"}` with `X-Logbook-Format: 2`. Conformance: I transcribed all six client `.g.dart` codecs into a checker, calibrated it against `client_sample_log.json` (0 issues), then ran the fixture through `logbook.Emit` and re-checked the emitted body — `0 decoder-fatal issues`, version 2. So the body decodes and the envelope does not.
findings.fix: As ruled — `logbookFormatVersion` → 2 on the client, before the first real request, and the client must SEND `X-Logbook-Format` so a future disagreement is a clean 406 rather than a quarantine. R1 already lists this as CLIENT-PREREQUISITES item 1; nothing to change in the plan, only to write.

findings.finding: It is EIGHTEEN, not four, and the four that were named are not even the four that exist in that shape. Counted with a command: fifteen 'Your log could not be saved, so X' sentences write to the LOG (a sixteenth, `settings_screen.dart:423`, is `preferences.json` and genuinely stays local and unaffected); two more assert the same outcome in different words ('was not added and your log is unchanged', 'The trip was not created and your log is unchanged'); and D3's 'The shared link stops working' is the revocation promise. Eighteen sentences across eleven screens — one per writing control, which is the cross-check that the count is right. Every one of the seventeen failure sentences asserts an OUTCOME a network write cannot guarantee, for exactly the reason v6 states. And the omission is a repeat of a named pattern: v4 corrected v3's misattribution of D3's 'stops working' from H1, and did not recount the set — so `delete_sheets.dart:608`, D3's OWN 'so nothing was deleted', on the sheet where the user types a trip's name to destroy it, is in neither list. That is CLAUDE.md rule 9's fourth instance verbatim: recount the whole table, not the row somebody names.
findings.evidence: `grep -rn 'could not be saved' lib/src/screens/ | grep -v '///' | wc -l` → 16 (one of which is preferences). `grep -rn 'your log is unchanged' lib/src/screens/ | grep -v '///'` → 2. `grep -rn 'stops working' lib/src/screens/` → 1. Sites, on `wipe/mock-data`: delete_sheets 165/366/608/649, share_sheet_screen 240, edit_sheets 383/453/514/603, edit_traveller_sheet 190, trip_screen 263, profile_screen 241, to_file_screen 101/102, add_city_screen 136/164, new_trip_screen 164, refile_photo_sheet 197.
findings.fix: Replace 'FOUR client sentences' with the eighteen, re-derived by the three commands above rather than transcribed, and split them into the three classes they actually fall into: (i) seventeen that assert an outcome, of which the honest replacement is retry-then-refresh over a genuinely unknown interval (DEC-33 makes every verb idempotent, so this is tractable); (ii) one, D3:649, that promises revocation and must be written against DEC-84's `S3_PRESIGN_TTL_PUBLIC = 15m`; (iii) `settings_screen.dart:423`, which needs NO change and should be named as excluded so a designer does not rewrite a sentence that is still true. Also note that the 'four' items and their line numbers were measured on `main`; on `wipe/mock-data`, the branch the client is going to, D2 is 366 not 367 and D3 is 608/649 not 609/650.

findings.target: internal/httpx/errors.go (twelve codes) × the client's single failure channel
findings.finding: The client's entire error model is `Future<bool>` out of `_commit`, and one fixed sentence per surface. Twelve codes collapse to one boolean, and three of them need behaviour the boolean cannot express: `unauthenticated` (the credential is dead — the answer is the sign-in screen, not 'your log could not be saved'), `unsupported_format` (PERMANENT — a client that retries it retries forever, which is the shape the brief attributes to `deleted`), and `invalid_field` (a client bug — retrying is the wrong answer and the `field` key is the only thing that says which). `rate_limited` and `timeout` are the two that SHOULD be retried and are indistinguishable from the others today. Separately: THE BRIEF'S PREMISE ON THIS POINT IS STALE. There is no `deleted` code — DEC-04 is WITHDRAWN in v3 ('the failure it managed CANNOT OCCUR'), and `grep -rn '"deleted"' internal/` returns nothing. The retries-forever hazard is real; it just belongs to `unsupported_format`.
findings.evidence: `internal/httpx/errors.go:47-60` (the twelve). Client: `logbook.dart:_commit` returns bool and never throws; the eighteen call sites read `ok` and set `_failed`. Live: `401 {"code":"unauthenticated"}`, `422 {"code":"invalid_field","field":"cityIds"}`, `406 {"code":"unsupported_format"}`, all measured. DEC-04: `docs/go-backend-plan-v6.json`, `"status": "WITHDRAWN in v3"`.
findings.fix: CLIENT-PREREQUISITES must carry the mapping explicitly, as a table of twelve rows, each answering the two questions CLAUDE.md already demands of every writing control — where the user stands afterwards, and what the screen says. The minimum is three lanes rather than one: RETRY (`rate_limited`, `timeout`, transport failure), REPORT (`invalid_body`, `invalid_field`, `conflict`, `payload_too_large`, `not_found`, `forbidden`, `internal`, `upload_incomplete`), and RE-AUTHENTICATE (`unauthenticated`). `unsupported_format` is its own lane and must never retry. `_commit` returning `bool` is not enough to carry that; the type change is part of the client work and should be named.

findings.target: DEC-46/DEC-47 × the five AssetImage accessors on branch wipe/mock-data
findings.finding: On the branch the client is going to, there are FIVE `AssetImage` constructions and ZERO declared assets — `pubspec.yaml` declares only `fonts`, and `assets/imagery/` is gone. After DEC-46 the argument to all five is a 64-hex object id, so `AssetImage('e66b…')` resolves nothing and `log_image.dart`'s failure plate draws instead. Every photograph, every trip cover, every city cover and every place cover in the app is a grey plate until DEC-47's object-id ImageProvider lands. That makes DEC-47 not an optimisation but the difference between an app with pictures and an app without, and it should be stated in those terms rather than as a cache-key argument. Two smaller corrections fall out: the client's own CLAUDE.md still says 'Sixteen AssetImage constructions across twelve files are EIGHT … five accessors and three fixture constants' — the three constants went with the fixture, so it is five; and the failure plate is deliberately SPOKEN-SILENT ('a picture that will not come is drawn, not spoken', because today a failure means a build defect), which stops being true the moment the source is a network fetch.
findings.evidence: `grep -rn 'AssetImage' lib/ | grep -v '\.g\.dart'` on `wipe/mock-data` → 5 hits: `place.dart:83`, `photo.dart:71`, `logbook.dart:1547`, `city.dart:97`, `trip.dart:79`. `ls assets` → `fonts` only. `ls lib/src/logbook/ | grep -i sample` → nothing.
findings.fix: Promote DEC-47's item with the consequence attached, not just the reason: 'without this, every image in the app is the failure plate.' Name the three answers the client's own record already lists as open and unchosen (a parameter on the accessor; a screen-level helper, which `ui/` may not have because it may not read a provider; or a provider mapping locator → ImageProvider) and say that this decision is now forced rather than deferred. Add that the failure plate's 'drawn, not spoken' decision needs re-examining, because a network miss IS something a user can act on.

findings.target: docs/CLIENT-PREREQUISITES.md — the file does not exist yet; R1 work item 6 is its only specification
findings.finding: The brief asks whether the handoff is complete and correct. It cannot be scrutinised because it has not been written — `find . -iname '*CLIENT*'` returns only `internal/logbook/testdata/client_sample_log.json`. R1's file list does create it, so this is an unwritten deliverable rather than a gap in the plan. Judged against R1's outline, five items are MISSING and one is already DONE. MISSING: (1) DEC-85's `shareLinkId` consequence — ruled minutes ago, and its own text says 'RECORD IT IN CLIENT-PREREQUISITES rather than letting the client phase discover it'; (2) DEC-84's number — R1 says 'DEC-56's four sentences' but DEC-84 supersedes it with `S3_PRESIGN_TTL_PUBLIC = 15m` as the sentence the copy must be written against, and the count is wrong (see the eighteen-sentence finding); (3) DEC-61's actual client consequence — R1 says 'the sign-in flow, which is two requests', which conflates it; the ruling is that REGISTER DOES NOT SIGN YOU IN, so it is register-then-session as two separate calls, and the first screen after registering must render a traveller with NO NAME; (4) the `refilePhoto` SIGNATURE CHANGE — `refilePhoto(photoId, placeId)` gains `visitId` and `visitAt` because the client mints both (v6 DEC-26 amendment, and the R7 route body is `{placeId, visitId, visitAt}`); this is a real change to one of the eighteen named methods and to `LogbookNotifier._freshId`'s role, at one call site, M2.2; (5) DEC-34's cache and the three things logout clears (cache document, byte cache, Keychain item). ALREADY DONE: R1's outline implies the fixture removal is pending — it is not. `wipe/mock-data` has already deleted `sample_log.dart` and `assets/imagery/`, and `main.dart`'s own comment records that the `sampleClock` override went with it ('There were four, and the fourth was the clock… The fixture is gone, so it has gone'). Listing it as work would send somebody to undo nothing.
findings.evidence: `ls docs/` — no CLIENT-PREREQUISITES.md. R1 work item 6 quoted in full from `docs/plan-v7.json`. Client `lib/main.dart` `startupOverrides` has three entries, not four, with the clock's removal documented in the doc comment above it. `grep -rn 'logbookNowProvider' lib/src/logbook/logbook.dart:906` → `DateTime.now().toUtc()`, unoverridden in `main()`.
findings.fix: Write it in R1 as R1 already schedules, adding the five items above and STRIKING the fixture/clock item (or restating it as 'already done on wipe/mock-data — verify, do not redo'). Two more that belong in it and are in nobody's list: `dio` is ALREADY a dependency (`pubspec.yaml`), so the HTTP client is not a seventh-package conversation — only `flutter_secure_storage` is; and the client's `logbook_store.dart` becomes a CACHE rather than a record, which retires the quarantine, the sidecar, S1's notice and U2's sidecar export line — v6 correctly calls that 'a simplification AVAILABLE to the client, not required', and it should be carried as such rather than as a task.

findings.finding: `instantLayout` is `…05.000`, three fractional digits, and Go TRUNCATES rather than rounds. Dart's `toIso8601String()` writes SIX digits whenever `microsecond != 0`, and `logbookNow` is `DateTime.now().toUtc()`, which has microsecond precision on the VM. So two of the six date-bearing fields can carry six digits from the client — `Photo.filedLater` (N1's Later: `logbookNow().add(filedLaterSnooze)`) and `Visit.at` when a refile mints one from `photo.takenAt`. Round-tripping them through the server truncates. The VALUE loss is harmless (sub-millisecond on a snooze deadline), but DEC-68's leg is 'one golden round-trip PER DATE-BEARING FIELD, asserting the emitted string is byte-identical to what the client sent' — and that leg passes on the fixture, which is all-millisecond, while failing on real client data. A leg whose premise the fixture cannot falsify is the thing this project's rule 9 is about.
findings.evidence: Measured: `Instant.UnmarshalJSON("2026-08-24T10:00:00.123456Z")` then `MarshalJSON()` → `"2026-08-24T10:00:00.123Z"`. Live, on a field that is NOT an Instant: `POST /v1/auth/session` → `"expiresAt":"2026-09-24T00:23:25.756360458Z"` — NINE digits, so the wire is already carrying three different fractional widths. Client: `to_file_screen.dart:89` `until: ref.read(logbookNowProvider).add(filedLaterSnooze)`; `logbook.dart:906` `DateTime.now().toUtc()`.
findings.fix: Either state the truncation as the contract (millisecond precision on the wire, and the client truncates before sending so the round trip IS byte-identical), or widen `instantLayout` to `.999999`. Prefer the first — it matches the client's own encoder for every value it has ever written. Whichever, the golden legs need at least one input the fixture does not contain: a six-digit fraction, and a zoneless string (see the date-zone blocker). `expiresAt` is outside DEC-68's six and should be named as such so nobody 'fixes' it into an `Instant`.

findings.finding: `POST /v1/auth/register` answers `{"id":…,"email":…,"name":null}`. The log's `traveller` object is `{"name":…}` and its codec is `Traveller(name: json['name'] as String)` — non-nullable. The two shapes share a key name and disagree on both its nullability and the surrounding object. A client that reuses `Traveller.fromJson` on the register response throws on the ordinary path, because DEC-61 rules that `name` IS null until `PATCH /v1/me`.
findings.evidence: LIVE: `POST /v1/auth/register` → `{"id":"4ef3d0d1-…","email":"…","name":null}` [201]. `traveller.g.dart:10-11`. The log's own traveller measured live as `"traveller": null` for the same nameless account, which the client handles correctly.
findings.fix: One line in CLIENT-PREREQUISITES: the register/session responses are their own types and must not be decoded with `Traveller.fromJson`. Worth stating because the key name invites it and the failure is a hard throw on the very first screen after sign-up.

findings.finding: Three date columns are scanned into `sql.NullTime` and then read unconditionally: `v.At = logbook.At(at.Time)`, `p.TakenAt = logbook.At(takenAt.Time)`, `w.RecordedOn = logbook.At(recordedOn.Time)`. `.Valid` is never checked. All three columns are NOT NULL today, so this is correct — but the NOT NULL is doing 100% of the work, and if any of them ever becomes nullable the emitter answers `0001-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`, which `DateTime.parse` accepts happily and every screen renders as a year-1 date rather than failing. Contrast the same file's careful `instantOrNil` for `filed_later`, `started_on` and `ended_on`, and the explicit `if lat.Valid && lng.Valid` for coordinates — the asymmetry reads as an oversight rather than a decision.
findings.evidence: `internal/postgres/logbook_store.go` readVisits (`v.At = logbook.At(at.Time)`), readPhotos (`p.TakenAt = logbook.At(takenAt.Time)`), readWalks (`w.RecordedOn = logbook.At(recordedOn.Time)`), against `instantOrNil(started)` in readTrips. Schema: `visits.at timestamptz NOT NULL`, `photos.taken_at timestamptz NOT NULL`, `walks.recorded_on date NOT NULL`.
findings.fix: Scan into `time.Time` directly rather than `sql.NullTime` on all three — the driver then errors on a NULL instead of the emitter inventing a date, and the NOT NULL constraint and the Go type say the same thing. One line each, no behaviour change today.

findings.finding: `walks.name` and `travellers.name` both carry `CHECK (… IS NULL OR … <> '')`, matching the client's rule that an empty name is refused rather than stored. The three free-text fields do not, and one of them has a drawn consequence: `setPhotoCaption` deliberately converts `''` to null because M2 guards both note blocks on `caption != null`, so an empty string arriving from the wire draws an empty note box with no way out of it — which is the exact state the client's own doc comment says it refuses to create. `places.plan` and `trips.summary` are the same shape with less visible fallout.
findings.evidence: `walks_name_present_ck` and `travellers_name_present_ck` exist in 0001; there is no `photos_caption_present_ck`, `places_plan_present_ck` or `trips_summary_present_ck`. Client: `logbook.dart` setPhotoCaption — `final value = next.isEmpty ? null : next;` with the reasoning in the doc comment above it.
findings.fix: Add the three CHECKs in 0003 for symmetry with the two that exist, or state in 0001's comment that they are deliberately absent and why. Either is fine; two of five having the constraint is what reads as an accident.

findings.finding: The client's collision guard is `log.holdsId(id)` against its OWN log, and its doc comment is emphatic that a duplicate is not cosmetic. Against a server that is the authority and a cache that can be stale, that guard no longer means what it says: `PUT /v1/trips/{id}` is an unconditional upsert with no exists-branch, so a colliding id silently OVERWRITES an existing trip rather than being refused. At 31^12 a random collision is not the risk; a stale cache is. It is genuinely small, and it is the one place the client's stated invariant stops holding without anything saying so.
findings.evidence: `logbook.dart:_freshId` and its doc comment ('Refused, not retried'). `internal/postgres/logbook_store.go` upsertTripSQL — `ON CONFLICT ON CONSTRAINT trips_pkey DO UPDATE SET …`, which is DEC-33's idempotency and is correct for a RETRY of the same write.
findings.fix: Name it in CLIENT-PREREQUISITES rather than changing anything: the upsert is right for idempotency and the local guard is now belt-and-braces, not the guarantee its comment claims. If it ever matters, the server side is a `WHERE NOT EXISTS` create/update split, and that is a DEC-33 conversation.

findings.target: definition_of_done — 'the emitted document equals the client's own fixture … Value for value, through the emitter'
findings.finding: Correct as written, and it will fail if anybody implements it as a byte comparison. Measured: the client wrote `"lat":-45.0` and Go emits `"lat":-45`. One place, `nz-wish-0` / Roys Peak, and it accounts for exactly 2 of the 2-byte length difference between the fixture and the re-emitted body. The values are equal as float64 and the client's `(json['lat'] as num).toDouble()` reads both, so nothing is wrong — but `types.go`'s claim that emit_test 'assert[s] the two documents are equal value for value' is true only of the decoded values, and the strongest-leg-in-the-project language around this round trip invites a byte diff.
findings.evidence: `json.Marshal(Emit(2, decoded))` over `client_sample_log.json`: 85,422 bytes in, 85,420 out. Diff: `"coordinates":{"lat":-45.0,"lng":168.6}` → `"coordinates":{"lat":-45,"lng":168.6}`, plus `"version":1` → `"version":2`. No other difference anywhere in the document.
findings.fix: Say 'decode both and compare the decoded values' in the definition_of_done, and cite `-45.0`/`-45` as the reason — it is the concrete case, it is in the reference document, and quoting it stops somebody 'fixing' the emitter to print `.0`.

verified_correct: NULLABILITY, EXHAUSTIVELY. I transcribed all six client `.g.dart` codecs into a checker, calibrated it against `client_sample_log.json` (0 issues), then ran that document through `logbook.Emit` and re-checked: 0 decoder-fatal issues. Every non-nullable Dart cast is met by a non-nullable Go field or an explicitly normalised one. The full non-nullable set the server must never send null for: Country.code/name, LatLng.lat/lng, City.id/name/country/centre, Logbook's five lists, Photo.id/tripId/cityId/takenAt/asset, Walk.id/tripId/cityId/recordedOn/distanceKm/points, Visit.id/placeId/tripId/at, Place.id/cityId/name/coordinates/visits, Trip.id/name/cityIds, Traveller.name.

TRAVELLER nil-vs-{}. `readTravellerName` answers nil for a NULL name, never an empty object. Measured live on a nameless account: `"traveller": null`, which `log.g.dart`'s `json['traveller'] == null ? null : …` handles. `{}` would have thrown on `json['name'] as String`.

NUMBERS. The client reads every coordinate and `distanceKm` as `(json[…] as num).toDouble()` and `accuracyMetres` as `(json[…] as num?)?.toInt()`. There is NO `as double` anywhere in `lib/` — `grep -rn 'as double' lib/` returns nothing. Demonstrated rather than asserted: Go emits `"lat":-45` for the fixture's one whole-numbered coordinate and the client's codec reads it.

THE SIX DATE-BEARING FIELDS ARE ALL `Instant`. trips.start, trips.end, walks.recordedOn, visits.at, photos.takenAt, photos.filedLater — six, matching the brief. `Instant.MarshalJSON` unconditionally `.UTC()`s and appends a literal `Z`, so all six render as `…T…:…:….000Z`.

THE THREE `date` COLUMNS ARE RE-RENDERED AS T00:00:00.000Z — DEC-68's emitter requirement, MEASURED through pgx and the live stack rather than read: `PUT /v1/trips/lens-dates` with `"start":"2027-10-12T00:00:00.000Z"` came back from `GET /v1/logbook` as `"start":"2027-10-12T00:00:00.000Z"`, so `DateTime.parse` hands the client a UTC value for a `date` column, not a local one.

LIST NORMALISATION ON THE DOCUMENT PATH. `Emit` normalises all five top-level lists plus every place's visits and every walk's points, so a query returning no rows cannot emit `null`. Measured live on an empty account: `"cities":[],"places":[],"photos":[],"walks":[]`. (The BARE-ENTITY path is a separate blocker above.)

cityIds ORDERING. `ORDER BY ordinal` on both the whole-log read and the single-trip re-read, ordinals written from array position in `replaceTripCities`, and the wire array is the client's travel order. Measured live: `"cityIds":[]` on a bare write response, i.e. `EmitTrip` is on the write path.

ID CHARSET. The client's `_idAlphabet` is `abcdefghjkmnpqrstuvwxyz23456789` — a strict subset of the server's `^[a-z0-9-]{1,64}$` and of `*_id_charset_ck`. Twelve characters, well inside 1..64. Both `newLogbookId` and `newShareLinkId` draw from it, so share tokens pass `share_links_token_present_ck` too.

ARITY: ALL 18 CLIENT WRITE METHODS MAP TO A ROUTE. deletePhoto→DELETE /v1/photos/{id}; removePlace(deletePhotos:)→DELETE /v1/places/{id}?photos=keep|delete; deleteTrip→DELETE /v1/trips/{id}; createTrip|renameTrip|setTripDates|setTripCities→PUT /v1/trips/{id}; createCity(attachTo:)→PUT /v1/cities/{id} (the attachTo cascade is one route, matching the client's one-commit rule); createPlace→PUT /v1/places/{id}; refilePhoto→POST /v1/photos/{id}/refile; setTravellerName→PATCH /v1/me; snoozeUnfiledPhotos→POST /v1/photos/snooze, which is the BULK route the client's group semantics need and the one place a partial-failure story would otherwise have appeared; dismissWalk|setWalkName→PUT /v1/walks/{id}; setPhotoCaption→PUT /v1/photos/{id}; setShareOptions→PUT /v1/trips/{id}/share; stopSharing→DELETE /v1/trips/{id}/share; newShareLink→POST /v1/trips/{id}/share. No client write is left without a route and no route has the wrong arity.

ENUMS AND SENTINELS: THERE ARE NONE ON THE WIRE. Every enum the client switches on is DERIVED, not decoded — `TripPhase` from dates, `PlaceStatus` from `visits.isEmpty`, `ToFileKind` and `PhotoLane` from the log's shape, `LogbookSource` from the store. No `switch` in `lib/` is driven by a wire value, so a new server-side enumerand cannot silently fall through a client branch. Worth recording so this row is answered rather than left silent.

COORDINATE PAIRING. `photos_coordinates_paired_ck CHECK ((lat IS NULL) = (lng IS NULL))` in the schema, and `if lat.Valid && lng.Valid` in `readPhotos`, together match the client's single nullable `LatLng?` — which cannot represent half a coordinate.

ETAG SAFETY FOR A NEW TRAVELLER. `tagFor` answers "" below version 1, so a never-written log serves 200 with NO ETag rather than `W/"1-0"`, and `ETagMatches` answers false for every If-None-Match including `*`. Measured: first read of a fresh account had no ETag; after one write, `ETag: W/"1-1"` and a conditional re-read returned `304` with 0 body bytes.

EMPTY-NAME SYMMETRY. `travellers_name_present_ck` and `walks_name_present_ck` match the client's deliberate refusals in `setTravellerName` and `setWalkName`, and the asymmetry with `setPhotoCaption` (which clears rather than refuses) is preserved by `photos.caption` being plain nullable text.

THE ENVELOPE SHAPE MATCHES. The server's `{version, logbook:{…}}` is exactly what `decodeLogbook` expects — a `version` it compares and a `logbook` object it hands to the generated codec. Only the version's VALUE disagrees; the structure does not.

questions_for_human: DEC-85's shareLinkId: is an additive `"shared": bool` on the emitted Trip acceptable? It restores H1's 'Stop sharing' from any device and leaks no capability, and by the client's own rule an additive field with a default does not move the format version. The alternative is that a shared trip becomes unrevocable from the phone after any rename — which is a bigger cost than DEC-85's text accounts for.

The date-zone blocker: does the client convert with `.toUtc()` before sending, or does `Instant.UnmarshalJSON` accept a zoneless string as UTC? (a) also changes what `logbook.json` holds on disk today; (b) makes the server guess at a string's meaning, which is the class of thing `logbookFormatVersion` exists to refuse. My recommendation is (a), with a server leg asserting a zoneless date is REFUSED.
